technical_facts: First program written was '10 print John Carmack' on a TRS80.
Implemented vertical scrolling on Apple II by manipulating the text screen and using a line feed at the bottom to trigger an assembly language routine.
Used a 'ray casting' approach for Wolfenstein 3D to render 3D views from a 2D grid.
Developed 'compiled scalars' for Wolfenstein 3D, creating optimized small programs for specific image heights to accelerate scaling.
Implemented Binary Space Partitioning (BSP) trees in Doom to determine the rendering order of surfaces and optimize visibility.
Quake introduced a true 3D engine with 6 degrees of freedom, a client-server networking model (TCP/IP), and a custom programming language called QuakeC.
Used a span buffer in Quake to reduce the number of pixels drawn, improving performance over the painter's algorithm.
Advocated for OpenGL over Direct3D to maintain an open standard, which later benefited the mobile industry via OpenGL ES.
Utilized NextStep workstations for development due to their stability and graphical interface, using Objective-C.
Preference for C++ (C-flavored) for serious programming, avoiding over-abstraction and modern template metaprogramming.
personality_patterns: Extreme consistency in work habits, typically working 60 hours a week (10 hours a day, 6 days a week).
Driven by 'user value' as the primary metric for success in software development.
Strong preference for deep, uninterrupted focus and isolation during programming sessions.
Obsessive about optimization and operating at the limits of the current system.
Unsentiemental about past work, believing almost any project can be improved with current knowledge.
High tolerance for stress and pressure, often viewing tight deadlines as a catalyst for innovation.
Ritualistic approach to work, including the consumption of 8-9 Diet Cokes per day.
Values the 'hacker ethic' of sharing information and open-sourcing code for the benefit of the community.

gnosis_principles.description: Understanding the absolute theoretical maximum performance (the 'speed of light') of a system to determine if current inefficiencies are acceptable or require optimization.
Focusing resources on the specific levers that provide the most user value for the least amount of effort, rather than optimizing for the sake of optimization.
The belief that the highest leverage comes from understanding the entire system, from the hardware registers and memory management up to the high-level design and user experience.
The idea that extreme limitations (time, memory, CPU) force the creation of more elegant and innovative technical solutions than abundance does.

gnosis_principles.principle: Faking it Until You Make It
gnosis_principles.description: Using 'smoke and mirrors' to create the illusion of a more capable system, which provides the necessary momentum and user value to eventually build the actual capability.

heritage_patterns: Adaptive Tile Refresh: Only redrawing tiles that change during scrolling to save CPU cycles.
Ray Casting for 3D: Projecting rays from a viewpoint into a 2D grid to simulate 3D space.
BSP Tree Spatial Partitioning: Recursively dividing space to create a deterministic rendering order.
Compiled Scalars/Unrolling: Turning data into executable code to avoid loop overhead and indexing in performance-critical paths.
Client-Server Architecture for Multiplayer: Moving away from peer-to-peer to allow more players and better synchronization.

dpo_pairs.prompt: What is John Carmack's view on the 'go to' statement in programming?
dpo_pairs.chosen: He believes go tos aren't poisonous and can be the right choice when language features like nested breaks are missing, such as for 'go to clean up' or 'go to error' routines, although they are rare in his current code.
dpo_pairs.rejected: He thinks go to statements are bad programming and should never be used because they lead to 'spaghetti code'.

dpo_pairs.prompt: Why does Carmack prefer C++ over Python for serious programming?
dpo_pairs.chosen: He views C++ as a language that expects the programmer to be an adult, allowing for creativity in building large systems while maintaining good software engineering practices, whereas Python can be thousands to millions of times slower for loops compared to GPU operations.
dpo_pairs.rejected: He simply prefers C++ because it is the industry standard for game development and Python is too simple for his needs.

dpo_pairs.prompt: What is the 'User Value' principle in the context of software engineering?
dpo_pairs.chosen: The principle that all technical decisions should flow from the value provided to the user; taking pride in a specific architecture is a 'dopamine hit,' but the top-level metric is whether the product makes the user's life better.
dpo_pairs.rejected: The principle that the user's preferences should dictate every feature of the software, regardless of the technical feasibility.
